title: Column header affordances, multi-sort chips & keyboard reflow for compact density
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: our table header interactions are inconsistent across density modes and break keyboard workflows in compact/very-compact row heights. This causes discovery issues for multi-column sort, unclear drag targets for column resize, and jitter during virtualized rerenders.

Goal: deliver a unified header affordance system that: 1) surfaces multi-sort state as compact chips; 2) provides a predictable, discoverable column resize drag target with expanded hit area but no visual clutter; 3) preserves keyboard-only reflow and focus order at each density mode; and 4) integrates with virtualization buffer logic so resizing/sorting does not cause scroll jumps.

Scope: design tokens (spacing, hit area, iconography), header micro-interactions (hover, focus, active), multi-sort chips (compact display + overflow menu), accessible drag handles with snap guides, keyboard reflow interactions (Shift+Arrow for column reorder, Alt+Arrow for resize step), and interaction guidance for engineers to implement without undermining batching/virtualization. Excludes: sticky column pinning UX changes and server-driven column schemas (handled elsewhere).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Multi-sort chips appear in header when 2+ sort columns are active and collapse gracefully at very-compact density; 2) Column resize has an invisible expanded hit area of at least 24px and shows a thin preview guide only while dragging; 3) Keyboard-only flows: Tab focuses header controls in a logical order; Shift+Arrow triggers reorder with animation; Alt+Arrow adjusts width in 8px steps and announces new width via aria-live; 4) No visible scroll jump or row flicker observed in integration prototype with virtualization buffer (prototype test build: table-demo/virtualization-v2); 5) Reduced-motion preference respected for animations; 6) Unit props and tokens documented in the design system page with code snippets and QA checklist.
notes:
Design trade-offs discussed: we prefer non-persistent visual handles to reduce visual noise in dense tables; this relies on a larger hit area which engineering must implement at the interaction layer (pointer-events zone) rather than visual elements. We chose 8px resize step to align with spacing token rhythm and avoid fractional layout thrashing. For multi-sort chips we use a single-row overflow with a +N indicator to avoid header wrap.

Accessibility: worked with accessibility consultant to ensure 1) focus visibility at low contrast; 2) ARIA attributes for reorder (aria-grabbed/aria-dropeffect fallback guidance); 3) live-region announcements for width and reorder. See checklist in artifacts.
